en: The Prophecy of Ajitasena.
Om, homage to the Omniscient One!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great saṅgha of twelve thousand five hundred bhikṣus, such as the venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya, the venerable Mahānāman, the venerable Revata, the venerable Vakkula, the venerable Śāriputra, the venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra, and millions of other disciples.

They all approached the place where the Blessed One was, at the Jetavana monastery; having bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they stood before him together with thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas,
such as the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartana, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Anikṣiptadhura, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Maitreya, and the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
And with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
and thirty-two thousand Bodhisattvas headed by these,
they all approached the place where the Blessed One was and where the Jetavana monastery was; having bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they stood before him.
Then, indeed, at the time of the forenoon, the Blessed One, having dressed himself and taking only his bowl and robe, entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Go, Ānanda, and bring the wheel-marked bowl and the carrying-net."
Then, as soon as he heard the Blessed One, the Venerable Ānanda brought his bowl, its stand, and his carrying-net to the Blessed One.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"When you enter for alms, O Mendicant, you liberate many living beings."
For you shall deliver many beings from the fear of hell and from the great fear of birth and old age.

O Leader of Men, you who possess great majesty and are worthy of the supreme gift, liberate us from the great terror of the mire of the suffering of saṃsāra; having liberated us, may you indeed come back again.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, having spoken these verses to the Blessed One, stood silent. Then the Blessed One stood not far from the great city of Śrāvastī.
Thereupon, all those windows, gate-towers, and balconies appeared made of gold, crystal, and silver.
Likewise, in the great city of Śrāvastī, a vast multitude of people had gathered.
Then that multitude became filled with doubt, wondering: "What is the cause, what is the reason that this auspicious omen has appeared for the city?
Lest this city be reduced to ashes!"
Then, within that assembly of people, there stood an elderly man, advanced in years, who had lived for many hundreds of thousands of millions of years.
Then that man, comforting the assembly of people, spoke as follows:
"Do not fear, O sons of good family!
In this very spot on earth is the monastery named Jetavana.

There dwells the Tathāgata named Śākyamuni—Arhat, Samyaksambuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans."
And the Buddha, the Blessed One,
entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
At the time of his arrival, this auspicious omen occurred.
Then that multitude of people, with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus to the aged man:
"Since this auspicious omen appeared at the time of proclaiming the qualities and praises of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One,
what kind of accumulation of merit will there be for one who has merely seen that Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One?"
Then that old man addressed the assembly of people with verses, proclaiming the praise of the Blessed One’s virtues:
"That person who hears the name of the Lord of the World shall be liberated from the sufferings of saṃsāra;
he shall never again go to the lower realms, and thus he will swiftly go to heaven."
Indeed, whoever hears the name of the Lord of the World with firm resolve throughout many millions of eons—
that Sugata of great majesty and noble self for inconceivable billions of trillions of eons—
that Bodhisattva remains as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; such a one never goes to the fear of the miserable realms.
Indeed, whoever hears the name of the Lord of the World shall never again be one who goes to the states of woe.
For inconceivable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons, he shall always be a universal monarch,
whoever should hold the name of the Lord of the World.
Whatever evil was previously committed, all of it will quickly go to destruction;
even Śakra, the lord of gods of great majesty, [will be purified] throughout inconceivable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons.
That bodhisattva goes to the buddha-field Sukhāvatī, seated cross-legged;
he possesses a Brahma-voice, a beautiful voice, and a gentle resonance that remains for billions of years.
"He who shall hold the name of the Lord of the World will never go to the states of woe.
Then that aged man, having proclaimed the praise of the Blessed One's virtues to the multitude of people, stood silent.
Thereupon, the Blessed One entered the great city of Śrāvastī through the eastern city gate.
And at that city gate, twelve koṭis of lotuses appeared;
upon those lotuses, twelve koṭis of bodhisattvas appeared, seated cross-legged with their palms joined in reverence.

Then, as soon as the Blessed One had entered the great city of Śrāvastī, nine hundred and ninety trillion beings were established in the world-system Sukhāvatī, and eighty-four hundred thousand billion beings were established in the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the world-system Abhirati.
Then the Blessed One arrived at the house of the girl Nagara-valambikā together with Ānanda.
Thereupon, the Blessed One caused his water-wheel to creak in the house of the girl Nagara-valambikā.
Then that girl, hearing the sound of the wheel, became filled with doubt.
"What is the cause? What is the reason that never before has a mendicant for alms come to my house?
Then that girl, the city-dweller, sat in an empty house, her throat choked with tears, weeping and lamenting; she remained there wailing and crying, searching for a sharp-edged sword.
She remained there.
Then that girl, sitting in the empty house, lamenting with a tearful throat and weeping, spoke in verses:
"Alas! What suffering in this poor household! Better for me to die than to live."
Moreover, what use have I for life amidst my duties, since my body is thus afflicted by suffering?
"Kana... where can there be protection or a final refuge? Today I have become one who is without a protector, since I was born into this very poor household.
(Asv 108) Then that maiden Nagara-valambikā, having sat in the empty house and spoken these verses, remained silent.
Then a son of the gods from the Śuddhāvāsa realm, standing in the midst of the sky, thought:
"If only the Blessed One would see this!
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who has practiced hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of manifold difficult deeds, is currently staying in the house of the girl Nagara-valambikā."

Then a son of the gods from the Śuddhāvāsa realm, taking a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold], a basket of food possessing a hundred flavors, and garments of Kāśī cloth, approached the house of the maiden Nagara-valambikā.
Then the son of the gods from the Śuddhāvāsa realm spoke thus to the maiden Nagara-valambikā:
“Daughter Prāvarā, put on these Kāśika garments and these ornaments worth many hundreds of thousands;
then, taking this pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand and this basket of food of a hundred flavors, present them to the Blessed One.

Then that girl, having put on those Kāśika garments, taken the pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, and taken that basket of food of a hundred flavors, approached the place where the Blessed One was.
Having approached, she presented her to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One said this to that Nagaravalambikā:

"Dārikā, dedicate [this merit] in the same manner as it was dedicated by the noble Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksambuddhas, such as Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and the rest."
"There will be an end to womanhood; there will be an end to poverty.
Then that girl, having dedicated that alms-food, offered it to the Blessed One.
"By this root of merit from the alms-food, may I never be reborn in any poor household.
Then that girl, the city-dweller, having dedicated that alms-food and given it to the Blessed One, began to depart for her own home.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to that girl, the city-dweller:
"Return, young lady!
I remember the causal basis of my former birth;
I shall relate it to you."
Then that girl, having turned back, prostrated herself before the Blessed One with a full-body obeisance.
Thereupon, the girl Nagara-valambikā addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"Surely it must be due to karma performed by me in the past, because of which I was born into a poor household."
Have compassion for me, who am suffering; O guardians of hell, turn back!
Show compassion for me, who am suffering, O Leader born in female form!
You, Lord of the World, deliver me from old age, disease, and grief—deliver me, who am so distressed.
Be my protection, my refuge, and my final resort; deliver me, who am suffering!
O Protector, you have indeed made this vow: "Whatever beings dwell here in Jambudvīpa, and all those beings who dwell in the ten directions, I shall bring them all to happiness."
And I shall deliver them all from the ocean of suffering; be our protection, our refuge, and our ultimate resort.
O Protector, surely this world has been delivered by you through my own past karma,
by which you have become a refuge for me, who was once born in a poor household and am now suffering.
But you, O Lord, are the deliverer from old age and disease, the refuge, the supreme one who has accumulated a mass of virtues;
I shall never again commit such evil deeds as those for which I now experience these sensations.
O Compassionate One, be born [for our sake]; O Supreme Being, become our protection, our refuge, and our final resort!
Whatever beings there may be here in Jambudvīpa, they shall indeed uphold your name in the future time.
After he has entered final nirvana, at a later time, when the teaching is on the verge of destruction,
whatever evil there may be— even that which was previously unknown— all of it shall quickly go to destruction.
Then that maiden Nagara-valambikā, having addressed the Blessed One in verse, set out once more toward her home.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to the maiden Nagara-valambikā with a voice whose resonance was like the song of the kalaviṅka bird:
"Return, girl; I remember the cause of my former birth, and I shall proclaim it.
Then that girl, having returned, spoke thus:
"O Leader of the World, proclaim today whatever extremely terrible sins were committed by me in the past."
Surely a most terrible sin was committed by me, because of which I am born into a poor household.
O caravan leader, liberate me here from this female state in all this world;
be my protection, my refuge, and my ultimate resort; O Leader, may I always be grateful to you.
Proclaim this guide to the Dharma to me; he shall never fall into an evil rebirth. Purify the karma as it was committed by me; be my protection, my refuge, and my ultimate resort.
O possessor of unimpeded wisdom, supreme leader of the world, I pay homage to you, O Protector; with palms joined in reverence, I take refuge in you.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to that girl:

"In the past, girl, in a time long gone, incalculable eons ago, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha named Ratnaśikhin, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed."
The Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. At that time, there was a royal capital named Padmāvatī.
Furthermore, at that time, in the royal capital of Padmāvatī, there was a householder named Padmaprabha.
You were the daughter of that householder Padmaprabha.
Now, at that time, a monk who lived on alms was entering the villages, towns, market-towns, and provinces to collect alms.
When he arrived at your house, you, young girl, having taken his alms-food, went out from the house and then entered it once again.
"And I shall not give alms to that wretched one with a shaven head.
By the accumulation of that karma, O girl, you have experienced sufferings again and again in the homes of the poor for twelve thousand kalpas.
Yet, by this single root of merit, O girl, you shall receive the prophecy of enlightenment."

"Since you have not seen that monk’s form, marks, or appearance, you, young lady, in a future time after inconceivable and immeasurable eons, shall become a Tathāgata named Nagara-dhvaja— an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One— in this world."
Then that girl, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, spoke thus:
"Blessed One, what will my buddha-field be like where I shall become a Buddha?
The Blessed One said:
That buddha-field shall be named Aparimitaguṇasañcaya;
and just as that world-system Sukhāvatī is, so shall that buddha-field be. The noble, spontaneously born bodhisattvas there shall be seated cross-legged.
Such was that buddha-field.
And yet, that girl—satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness—set out for her own home.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to that girl:
"Daughter, on the seventh day you will pass away. Having passed away,
in the eastern direction, in the realm of Magadha, there is a king named Ajitasena."
King Ajitasena has a harem of one thousand women.
Furthermore, a son shall be born to that King Ajitasena;
this will indeed be your final dwelling in a womb.
Then the Blessed One departed from the great city of Śrāvastī through the western city gate and proceeded toward the Jetavana monastery.
When the Venerable Ānanda saw the Blessed One approaching from afar, he bowed his head at the Blessed One’s feet, circumambulated him three times, and addressed the Blessed One in verse:
“O you of golden hue, adorned with the excellent marks, the bearer of the form endowed with the twenty-two marks!”
When you have come here, having liberated all sentient beings from their alms-food begging.

You have established all sentient beings in happiness; the power of loving-kindness has been exercised by you throughout the entire world. O supreme leader, by means of this alms-food, the world has been liberated from fear.
All those bodhisattvas here in Jambudvīpa who show you the path shall always uphold this sūtra praised by the Buddha during the time after you have entered parinirvāṇa.
After you have entered parinirvāṇa, in a future time when the teaching is being destroyed,
one will uphold this method, this jewel of a sūtra.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, having spoken these verses, circumambulated the Blessed One three times and stood before him. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Go, Ānanda, strike the ghaṇṭā."
Those disciples will partake of the alms-food.
Then the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, what kind of root of merit will the sound of the gong produce?"
The Blessed One said:
"Listen, Ānanda, I shall proclaim the root of merit of the sound of the gong.
Whatever beings, Ānanda, shall hear the sound of the gong, their five deeds of immediate retribution will be completely exhausted."
"They shall become irreversible and will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda said,
"Blessed One, what kind of roots of merit have those beings planted?"
The Blessed One said:

"Listen, Ānanda! Those beings who, in the future time, in the final age, when I have passed into parinirvāṇa and the true Dharma is being destroyed—at the time of the disappearance of the true Dharma—in villages, towns, market towns, districts, kingdoms, and royal capitals..."

“Ānanda, those beings who hear the sound of the gong being struck in a forest hermitage and shall utter ‘Homage to the Buddha,’ their five deeds of immediate retribution will be completely exhausted. Such, Ānanda, are the roots of merit of the sound of the gong.”
Then the Venerable Ānanda struck the ghaṇṭī with a voice that was calm and profoundly serene. Then, by the sound of that ghaṇṭī, all those great śrāvakas assembled;
as they sat down upon their seats, they partook of the alms-food.
Then, right there in the midst of the disciples, a great disciple named Nandimitra was present and seated.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Nandimitra, the great disciple:
"Go, Nandimitra, great disciple, to the eastern direction in the realm of Magadha, and perform the service of attending upon the spiritual friend of King Ajitasena."
Then the great disciple Nandimitra said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, we shall not be able to go to that region of the earth;
those beings are difficult to approach."
"They will deprive me of my life.
Then the Blessed One said this to the venerable Mahāśrāvaka Nandimitra:
"Those beings will not be able to move even a single hair on your head, much less deprive you of your life."

Then, at the time of dawn, the great disciple Nandimitra, having put on a golden-colored robe, set out toward the eastern direction, where the capital city of King Ajitasena was located in the kingdom of Magadha. Then, upon seeing the great disciple Nandimitra, King Ajitasena became pleased, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with a sense of gladness and happiness.
Then King Ajitasena dispatched a minister, saying,
"Go and bring this monk here.
Thereupon, that minister approached the great śrāvaka Nandimitra.
Then that minister said this to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"Come, great śrāvaka monk; the king commands you.
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra spoke thus to the minister:
"What business do I have with the king? What will the king do for me? Then the minister approached King Ajitasena and spoke thus to him.
And that bhikṣu did not come into your presence.
Then King Ajitasena dispatched five hundred ministers,
yet that bhikṣu did not [come] to the king.
He approached the side of Jitasena.
Then that king, in his very own physical form, went to where the great śrāvaka Nandimitra was;
having approached him, he spoke thus with palms joined in reverence:
"Come, O Bhikṣu, enter my royal capital.
Then King Ajitasena, taking the Bhikṣu by his right hand, entered his own royal capital. Thereupon, King Ajitasena offered a lion-throne to the Bhikṣu Nandimitra.
Then King Ajitasena, having sat down upon a noble throne, spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"Where are you going, monk? What is the cause? What is the reason?"
Then the great disciple Nandimitra spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Whosoever have gone forth as monks, they all subsist on alms-food and consume it while wandering for alms.
Then King Ajitasena spoke thus to that great disciple Nandimitra:
"Enjoy almsfood in my house;
I shall provide you with almsfood for as long as I live.
If you have need of my own flesh, O monk, I shall give you my own flesh."
Then the great disciple Nandimitra addressed King Ajitasena in verses:
"I shall eat this food which you give—exquisite food and drink, a beverage of supreme flavor.
For you shall be liberated from the afflictions; having attained this human birth, so difficult to find, you have achieved what is most rare."
The teaching of the Leader is extremely difficult to encounter; supreme faith and serene confidence are extremely difficult to encounter.
Those who have gone forth as monks within the teaching—the teaching of the Leaders—is extremely difficult to encounter.
The sight of the most excellent Sugata is very difficult to obtain; homage be to you, O Buddha of great majesty!
Homage be to you, O Great Sage composed of the Dharma; homage be to you, O Noble One skilled in overcoming the afflictions!
Homage be to you, who grant liberation from all old age! Homage be to you, the noble one who reveals the path!
Homage be to you, the guide of the way! Homage be to you, the revealer of the path to enlightenment!
Then the great disciple Nandimitra, having proclaimed the praise of the Blessed One’s virtues to King Ajitasena, remained silent.
Then the great disciple Nandimitra addressed King Ajitasena with these verses:
"The sight of a monk is very difficult to obtain; likewise, the sight of him would be very difficult to encounter."
To one who gives a gift to the community of monks, neither yakṣas nor rākṣasas [can cause harm].
Neither pretas, kuṣmāṇḍas, nor mahoragas ever create obstacles for those who give gifts to the saṅgha of monks; for that attainment of human birth is very difficult to obtain.

He who maintains the name of the Lord of the World for inconceivable billions of nayutas of kalpas— [he] who has obtained this state of a monk, the sight of which is difficult to find and most rare even in hundreds of inconceivable kalpas.
He who beholds such a king of monks shall never go to a state of ruin or an evil rebirth;
for him who beholds such a king of monks, there shall be no falling into ruin or an evil rebirth.
He who is my spiritual friend and the guide to my path— he has come for my alms;
indeed, those who give him alms shall be liberated and shall no longer suffer from old age or disease.
But those who shall give him alms-food here will always be liberated from the afflictions.
Then King Ajitasena, having extolled the praise of the virtues of the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, remained silent.
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"So be it, Great King; I shall eat alms-food in your house.
Then King Ajitasena satisfied the great śrāvaka Nandimitra with various kinds of hard and soft foods.
Thereupon, the great śrāvaka Nandimitra spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Great King, do you have a pleasure grove in this region of the earth?
The king replied, "Yes, Great Śrāvaka, I have a pleasure grove that is delightful and most beautiful."
Nandimitra said,
"I shall go, O Great King;
I will visit that park."
The king said:
"Go, Nandimitra;
inspect the park grounds."
Then the great disciple Nandimitra approached the park grounds of King Ajitasena.
Now, in those park grounds, all the qualities of a park were present:
the summer lotus ponds were filled with cool water, and the monsoon ponds were filled with water that was neither too warm nor too cold.
And those lotus ponds are covered with golden stairways, divine and delightful;
all those qualities of enjoyment found in Jambūdvīpa are present there,
as are flowers such as the *adhimuktaka*, *campaka*, *aśoka*, *mucilinda*, *pāṭala*, *sumanā*, and *saugandhika*.
(Asv 120) Those birds belonging to the animal realm—parrots, mynas, ruddy geese, peacocks, cuckoos, and so forth—uttered various cries.
Then, right there in that garden grove, birds appeared with golden-colored bodies, golden beaks, golden wings, and golden feet;
they all emitted the sound of "Buddha."
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra approached the royal capital of King Ajitasena. Thereupon, King Ajitasena spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"Have you come, O great śrāvaka?"
"The park grounds have been seen.
Nandimitra said, "I have seen the park grounds; they are delightful and very beautiful."
Then King Ajitasena addressed the great disciple Nandimitra with these verses:

"In Jambudvīpa there were various flowers for enjoyment: the *adhimuktaka*, the *campaka*, the *dhānuṣkārika*, the *aśoka*, the *mucilinda*, as well as the *pāṭala*, the *saugandhika*, the *sumanā*, and the *vārṣikā*."
Then the Pāriyātra mountain, situated on the riverbank, became golden-hued and was constantly filled with birds;
and they showed the way toward supreme enlightenment,
divine, charming, and sweet-voiced.
And they shall cause it to be heard at all times.
Then the great disciple Nandimitra, having spoken these verses to King Ajitasena, remained silent.
Then King Ajitasena struck the drum.
Then, gathered together by the sound of that drum, the assembly of ministers spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"For whose sake, Great King, has the drum been beaten?
Then the king said, "Let the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots be made ready."
"I shall go to the park grounds for the sake of recreation.
Then, having heard those words, the millions of ministers quickly made ready the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots.
Thereupon, in a mere instant, a brief moment, or a flash, King Ajitasena proceeded to where the park grounds were located.
And that great śrāvaka Nandimitra approached King Ajitasena and spoke to him thus:
"Great King, a small hut should be built by you on this spot of ground, where I may sit and partake of alms-food in your house.
Then King Ajitasena spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"What kind of hut should be built for you?
Nandimitra said,
"O Great King, build a hut such as corresponds to the great resolve, faith, and serene confidence that you possess."
Then King Ajitasena spoke thus to his chief minister:
"Have a hut built right on this very spot of earth.
Then the chief minister spoke thus to the king:
"Great King, what kind of hut should I have built?
King Ajitasena replied thus:
"Have a hut built thirty yojanas in length and six yojanas in height, made of the seven precious gems and covered with jewels and pearls."
Then that minister had a small hut constructed;
having had it made out of the seven precious gems and covered with jewels and pearls, he approached King Ajitasena and spoke to King Ajitasena as follows:
"Great King, I have constructed the hut exactly as you commanded.
The king said,
"On that very spot of ground, a walking path (caṅkrama) should be constructed, four yojanas in length and two yojanas in width."
Then that minister, having had that walkway constructed, approached King Ajitasena and addressed him with these verses:
"I have well and beautifully prepared this walkway, just as you previously commanded.
It shall liberate beings from their nature—both the auspicious and the inauspicious—and it shall set all these living creatures free."
Oh, how well-gained is what you have vowed! You shall liberate the entire world together with its gods.
Since you have made such a vow, may this Dharma-preacher proclaim the Dharma for me.

Having sat down, you established a small hut and a walking path; whatever was commanded by you, exactly as it was done, that very walking path was made most beautiful, and that ground was covered with precious jewels.
Then King Ajitasena departed for his own royal capital.
Thereupon, the great śrāvaka Nandimitra returned and sat down right there in that very hut; he entered the bodhisattva-samādhi called Vikiraṇa.

With one [hand] he reached for his hair, with another his nose, with another his teeth, with another his neck, with another his arms, with another his heart, with another his belly, with another his thighs, with another his shanks, and with another his feet; thus he was occupied with each part.
Then, after seven days had passed, King Ajitasena did not see that monk.
Thereupon, the king spoke thus to his eldest son:
"Come, noble son, I shall go to that hut;
I will approach that monk.
Then the king, together with his son, went to where that hut was located.
Then King Ajitasena, seeing that monk’s body cut into pieces, was seized by doubt;
his hair standing on end with terror, tearing at his clothes, lamenting and weeping with a choked voice, he spoke thus to his son:
"Bring me, my son, a sharp-edged sword."
"I shall deprive myself of life.
Then the prince, with palms joined in reverence, addressed the king in verses:
"O Lord of Men, do not let your mind be filled with grief; do not experience such a feeling as this."
Having committed suicide, you will go to hell;
indeed, you will go to the most dreadful Raurava hell.
This one is worthy of offerings in the world, for he is the liberator from old age and disease;
yet he was not slain by yakṣas, nor by bhūtas, nor by rākṣasas.
This Bodhisattva too is the liberator from old age and disease in the world.
He is worthy of offerings in this world, the liberator from old age and disease;
rare is the sight of him who shows the path to awakening.
The cause for your arrival was a spiritual friend;
he is one worthy of offerings in this world, who brings happiness to all sentient beings.
To the omniscient one who has reached the perfections, sent by the Lord of the World—
the Great Seer, the Lord of the World, possessed of firm vigor and steadfast power.
Whoever upholds its name shall not go to an evil destiny;
they shall not go to the states of woe, but for their rebirth in the heavenly world.
Then that prince, having spoken this verse to his father, remained silent.
Thereupon, King Ajitasena said to his own son:
"How do you know, O prince, that this monk had entered into meditative absorption?"
Then the prince spoke thus:

"Behold, Great King, this monk has entered the bodhisattva-samādhi; he is completely liberated from all afflictions, has reached the further shore of the ocean of existence, and for the sake of the welfare of all beings, he demonstrates the auspicious path."
Then the prince said this to the king:
"Come, father, let us go for a walk.
Thereupon, the king and the prince went together with many hundreds of boys to where that walk was located.
Then that monk, having emerged from that meditative absorption, spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Come, Great King; what are you doing in this place?
Then the king, seeing the monk, gave his crown-ribbon to the prince.
"Let your kingdom be yours; protect it according to the Dharma, not through unrighteousness.
The prince said:
I have performed many countless royal duties,
yet I have never known satisfaction.
O father, let the kingdom be yours.
"I have no need for the kingdom, nor for enjoyments, nor for sovereignty or lordship.
Let the kingdom be yours, dear father;
I shall protect it according to Dharma, not through unrighteousness."
Then the king approached that monk and, with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus:

"O Noble One, the sight of you is very difficult to obtain; O Leader, facing you with palms joined, I behold the arrival of liberation. O Noble One, the sight of you is very difficult to obtain even through hundreds of inconceivable deeds."
Those sages who shall grant you their vision will be liberated for ten million eons;
whoever hears your name for even a moment shall never go to the miserable states of ruin.
The king said:
"Seated upon a beautiful, precious chariot, I shall go to that royal capital.
I shall give abundant food; I shall give these garments of Kāśī cloth."
And these fine, closely woven nets of cloth which I give to you as a robe today.
Then that monk, taking a palanquin made of jewels, approached the royal capital.
Having been fully satisfied with food,
the great disciple Nandimitra addressed King Ajitasena in verses:

Those who give to the community of monks a gift of abundant food— excellent, pure, and consisting of the finest flavors of delicious drinks and meals— and thereby satisfy them, shall reach the seat of awakening before long.
The sight of the Leader is extremely difficult to obtain; before long, he will go to the Buddha-field.
He will swiftly go to Sukhāvatī, the excellent Buddha-field of Amitāyus.
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, having spoken these verses to King Ajitasena, remained silent.
Then King Ajitasena struck the drum.
Then, by the sound of that drum, all those tens of millions of ministers spoke thus to the king:
"For whose sake, Great King, has the drum been beaten?
The king replied,
"On the seventh day, the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots shall be made ready."
"On the seventh day, I shall go to the monastery named Jetavana to see, pay homage to, attend upon, and hear the Dharma from the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha. Then,
ten million ministers said this to King Ajitasena:
"Great King, we have prepared the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots.
Then King Ajitasena, having descended from his elephant-chariot and having helped the great śrāvaka Nandimitra descend from his jewel-encrusted chariot, proceeded toward the Jetavana monastery.
Then the Blessed One, seeing King Ajitasena approaching from afar, addressed all the śrāvakas.
"All must display various miraculous transformations.
Then all those great śrāvakas entered the bodhisattva-samādhi called Jvālāmāla (Flame-Wreath).
Then the king, seeing that Jvālāmāla from afar, spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"For whose sake do I see this mountain become garlanded with flames?
Nandimitra replied,
"The Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksambuddha, dwells here, maintains himself, and teaches the Dharma."
And those bodhisattvas had entered the bodhisattva-samādhi called Jvālāmāla (The Garland of Flames).
Then King Ajitasena, having descended from his elephant-chariot, approached the Blessed One on foot together with his thousand sons.
At that time, the Blessed One was walking about with a body the color of gold and a radiance extending one fathom.
Then King Ajitasena, having beheld the Blessed One’s physical form, color, marks, and proportions, fainted and fell to the ground.
Then the Blessed One, extending his gold-colored arm, raised the king up.
"Arise, Great King! For what reason have you fallen? The king said:
Throughout many inconceivable eons and hundreds of millions of inconceivable births,
I have never before seen you here in this world, the Lord of the World, the one most worthy of supreme offerings.
O Caravan Leader, you who liberate from old age and disease, golden-hued one whose limbs are adorned with excellent marks;
O Sage, he who bears the thirty-two marks shall never go to the realms of misfortune—he who beholds the form of the Lord of the World. Therefore, O Lord of the World, I bow my head in homage to you.
Then King Ajitasena, with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, I shall go forth into homelessness in your teaching.
Thereupon, the Blessed One was pleased, uplifted, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness.
To those who had not yet attained [the goal] there, so that my teaching might spread widely, he spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Go, Great King; on the seventh day from now, I shall come to your home."

Then King Ajitasena, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and cheerfulness, having placed that virtuous friend, the bhikṣu, before him, went to his own palace and addressed all his ministers:
"All the villages, towns, market towns, and provinces must clear the road; in every house banners must be raised, and in every house [ornaments] made of jewels."
The water-jars were to be filled.
Then all those ministers gave the order;
the roads were cleared by all the villages, towns, market-towns, and provinces, banners were raised, and jars made of jewels were filled.
Where King Ajitasena dwelt, there twelve koṭis of banners were raised and twelve koṭis of jeweled jars were filled.

Then, on the seventh day, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha— surrounded and escorted by a great saṅgha of senior disciples headed by Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, Ānanda, and Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra— arrived at the royal capital of King Ajitasena.
Then King Ajitasena, taking a basket of flowers and placing his spiritual friend before him, scattered flowers over the Blessed One and addressed the Blessed One thus:
"By this root of merit, may all sentient beings attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Then King Ajitasena prepared seats.
A lion throne was offered to that Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, seated upon the lion throne, taught the Dharma to King Ajitasena.
Thereupon, King Ajitasena gratified him with abundant food, both solid and soft.
Then King Ajitasena gave his eldest son, the prince, saying:
"Ordain this prince;
I shall go forth later."
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:
"Go, Ānanda, and ordain this prince.
Thereupon, the venerable Ānanda ordained that prince.
As soon as he had gone forth into homelessness, he attained the fruit of arhatship.
He beheld all the buddha-fields.
Then, standing in the air, the prince addressed his father with these verses:
Do not delay, dear father; do not feel any grief—you shall go somewhere.
Oh, how well-gained is the sight of the Sugatas! Oh, how well-gained is the attainment of the Sugatas!
Oh, what a supreme gain has been well-obtained—the attainment of the going-forth praised by the Sugata!
Liberation from saṃsāra was praised by the Sugata; having gone forth, do not delay, my dear father!
Do not cause distress to the Lord of the Leaders of the World; having obtained this human birth which is so very difficult to find, the sight of the Leaders is likewise very difficult to obtain.
For I have quickly gone forth into homelessness, and I have attained the supreme, foremost enlightenment.
Having heard those words of his son at that time, the king went forth into homelessness in the teaching of the Guide.
Then the prince, having ascended into the air and spoken this verse, remained silent.

Thereupon, King Ajitasena, having heard his son’s words, was satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness; he caused a monastery to be built for the sake of the Blessed One.
Ten million musical instruments were presented to her;
within her thousandfold inner court, her female organs vanished and male organs appeared.
Then King Ajitasena went forth into homelessness in the teaching of the Blessed One.
Those tens of millions of ministers went forth in the teaching of the Blessed One,
and those thousands of men from the inner court also went forth.
Having caused King Ajitasena to go forth, the Blessed One set out for the Jetavana monastery.
Then the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One in this way:
"This King Ajitasena, having renounced his kingdom and caused a monastery to be built, has gone forth in the teaching of the Blessed One.
What kind of root of merit will he possess?"
The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, Ānanda! That which you have proclaimed is true:
this King Ajitasena will go forth into homelessness within my teaching."

In a future time, after immeasurable, inconceivable, and limitless eons, there will appear in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ajitaprabha— one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.
Ānanda said:
"This great śrāvaka Nandimitra has been a spiritual friend to the king;
what kind of roots of merit will he possess?"
The Blessed One said:
"Ānanda, at that very time, this great śrāvaka Nandimitra will appear in the world as a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksambuddha named Nandiprabha.
Ānanda said:
"Blessed One, what will the buddha-field of those Tathāgatas be like?
The Blessed One said,
"That buddha-field where these Tathāgatas will appear shall be named *Aparimitaguṇasañcaya* (The Accumulation of Immeasurable Qualities)."
Ānanda said:
"What kind of mass of merit will belong to one who, in the final age, in the final time, shall fully proclaim this entire dharma-discourse?
The Blessed One said:
Ānanda, when I have awakened to enlightenment after practicing hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of difficult deeds, then those beings will awaken to enlightenment.
Those beings who hear even a single four-line verse from this Dharma-discourse shall become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda said:
"What kind of roots of merit will those Dharma-preachers possess who shall fully proclaim this Dharma-discourse?
The Blessed One said, "Listen, Ānanda: they will become universal monarchs (cakravartin), lords of the four continents."

Those who shall fully proclaim this Dharma-discourse in its entirety will become liberated; they will be freed from birth, old age, sickness, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair. Ānanda said:

“Blessed One, what will be the destiny of those beings in the future time, in the final age, who reject this Dharma-discourse and do not believe in it? What will be their refuge? The Blessed One said, “Enough, enough, Ānanda!”
"Do not question me regarding my mass of evil karma;
it is impossible for me to describe it fully,
nor indeed can it be described even by ten million Buddhas."
Ānanda said, "Proclaim it, Blessed One! Proclaim it!
The Sugata, the Blessed One, said:
Listen, Ānanda, I shall proclaim the destiny of one who rejects the true Dharma.

He must experience suffering for many thousands of eons in the Raurava great hell, the Hāhaha great hell, the Avīci great hell, in the animal realm, in the world of Yama, and in the domain of the hungry ghosts.
If he should ever be reborn in the human world, his mouth and throat will be long and parched.
His tongue will be twelve yojanas long,
and it will extend for twelve hundred yojanas for those who speak such words:
"O sons of good family, do not ever reject the true Dharma!"
"Such is the destiny of one who rejects the true Dharma. Ānanda asked,
"By what cause, Blessed One, is the true Dharma rejected?"

The Blessed One said: "Those beings who, in the future time, in the final age, shall revile, scold, despise, and disparage these Dharma-preachers who uphold these sūtras, and who shall give rise to malicious thoughts toward that Dharma-preacher— "
The true Dharma will be rejected by those beings. (Asv 134)
If one were to pluck out the eyes of all sentient beings in a triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system, the mass of demerit resulting from that would be even greater than this.
In the same way, whoever looks upon these upholders of the sūtra and preachers of the Dharma with a malicious mind will produce a mass of demerit far greater than that.
Then Ānanda addressed the Blessed One in verse:
I have heard many thousands of sūtras in the presence of the Teacher,
yet never before have I heard a sūtra such as this.
In the terrifying future time after the Teacher has entered parinirvāṇa,
I shall proclaim this sūtra and uphold this method.
In this jewel of a sutra, which shall exist in a future time,
I will provide protection for them in that most terrifying later age.
"I shall reject this; it was not spoken by the Buddha, for it is profound."
Then the venerable Ānanda, having spoken these verses to the Blessed One, remained silent.
Then the great disciple Kāśyapa addressed the Blessed One with verses:
"The Victor, golden-hued, whose limbs possess the excellent marks, who bears the thirty-two marks."
This well-spoken sutra, which possesses great power, is profound in dharma, subtle, and very difficult to perceive.
This unsurpassed sutra has been revealed; after the Victorious One has entered parinirvāṇa in the future time, I shall uphold this unsurpassed method of the sutra.
Then the Venerable Śāradvatīputra addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"Homage be to you, O Buddha of great majesty! This unsurpassed sūtra has been revealed by you.
O Leader of the World, after you have entered final nirvāṇa, this unsurpassed sūtra will be written down."
Nor does he go to the fear of miserable rebirths; rather, he goes swiftly to heaven.
Then the Venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"You are grateful to many beings and their deliverer from the fear of miserable rebirths.
By you this profound sūtra, the right-hand path of the Buddhas, has been revealed."
"For in the final age, when you, the Leader, have entered parinirvāṇa, I shall proclaim this sutra for the benefit of all living beings."
Thus it was said.
Then Brahmā Sahāmpati addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"Homage be to you, O Buddha of great majesty; this auspicious sūtra has been revealed by you. (Asv 136)
O Leader of the World, once you have entered final nirvāṇa, I shall provide protection for this jewel of a sutra.
Then the four great kings addressed the Blessed One in verses: "Aha! This most delightful jewel of a sublime sūtra has been revealed in such a way during this final age...
[he] beholds this jewel of a sūtra revealed in the final age."
"I shall indeed uphold this jewel of a sūtra of the Sugatas, the guides of the world;
I shall provide protection for this jewel of a sūtra. Thus spoke the Blessed One, his mind filled with joy.
And that entire assembly rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
Thus ends the Mahāyāna sūtra titled "The Exposition of the Prophecy of Ajitasena."

This is the religious gift of Bālosiṃha, together with his wife Jājatitrana; together with his parents, who were his greatest benefactors; together with Kṣīṇīena, Akhiloṭiena, Diśoṭajāja Maṅgali..., Uttrayannagarvidoṭiena, Vaṭrari-khuśoṭi, and Khūśogoṭiena, along with all sentient beings and all [deceased] ancestors, wherever that merit may reside—for the sake of the unsurpassed [enlightenment] of all sentient beings—along with his supreme spiritual friend and steadfast kinsman, Sthirabandhu.
This book was written by the Dharma-preacher Narendradatta.
